2.title: Two hellos
2.blurb: By the end you can greet people (formal and informal), say goodbye, introduce yourself and ask someone's name.

cards.def: the word you say when you meet someone
a short, friendly way to say hello
the greeting for the early part of the day
cards.example: ___! It's eight o'clock.

cards.def: the word you say when you leave
cards.example: ___! See you tomorrow.

cards.def: a friendly goodbye when you will meet again
cards.example: I'm going home now. ___!

cards.def: polite words you say when you meet a person for the first time
cards.example: This is my friend Ali. — ___.

cards.def: the word that people call you, for example Anna
cards.example: My ___ is Aigerim.

cards.def: a word you say when someone helps you
cards.example: Here is your coffee. — ___!

cards.def: also; as well
cards.example: Nice to meet you ___.

cards.def: words you use to introduce a person
a short way to say I am before your name
the question you ask to learn a person's name
cards.example: ___ — My name is Sam.

5.title: The family group chat
5.blurb: By the end you can talk about your family and use my / your / his / her and 's (Anna's mother).

cards.def: the people close to you: parents and children
cards.example: I have a big ___: three brothers and two sisters.

cards.def: your parents: dad and mum
cards.example: My ___ is a doctor. He is fifty.

cards.def: a boy and a girl with the same parents as you
cards.example: My ___ is a boy. He is ten.

cards.def: the children of a mother and father
cards.example: They have one ___ and one daughter.

cards.def: two married people: the man and the woman
cards.example: She is married. Her ___ is an engineer.

cards.def: your mother and father, and their parents
cards.example: My ___ are my mother and my father.

cards.def: the young people in a family; one of them is a child
cards.example: They have three ___: two boys and a girl.

cards.def: having a husband or a wife
cards.example: She is ___. Her husband's name is Ali.

cards.def: words you use to show your family: This is my sister
cards.example: ___ sister. Her name is Aida.

1.title: Rules of the Conversation
1.blurb: Question types \u2014 subject, object and indirect questions

cards.def: making you feel embarrassed or uncomfortable
cards.colloc: an awkward silence · feel awkward · an awkward question
cards.example: Stand too close and you might make someone feel ___.

cards.def: to say something while another person is speaking, so that they stop
cards.colloc: interrupt a person · sorry to interrupt · constantly interrupt
cards.example: We need to be aware of whether it’s OK to ___ a person.

cards.def: a situation in which somebody understands something in the wrong way
cards.colloc: lead to a misunderstanding · clear up a misunderstanding
cards.example: Getting these things wrong can lead to ___.

cards.def: to say or do something that makes somebody upset or angry
cards.colloc: offend somebody · cause great offence · be easily offended
cards.example: There are a few common gestures which can ___ people in some countries.

cards.def: to talk so much that other people cannot join in
cards.colloc: dominate the conversation · let somebody else speak
cards.example: I don’t like the way she always ___.

cards.def: a movement of the hands or head that carries a meaning
cards.colloc: make a gesture · a rude gesture · the meaning of a gesture
cards.example: I’d like to talk about ___ – the signs we make with our hands.

cards.def: to talk politely about unimportant things
cards.colloc: make small talk · be good at small talk
cards.example: Could you tell me how easy you find it to ___?

cards.def: to show clearly that you are interested in what somebody is saying
cards.example: It would be good if you tried to ___ in conversations.

cards.def: to have a short, loud argument
cards.colloc: have a row about money · have a row with somebody
cards.example: I don’t want to ___ about the weather.

cards.def: to reach moments in a conversation when nobody knows what to say
cards.colloc: have some awkward silences · fill an awkward silence
cards.example: When he asked how much we earned, we ___.

cards.def: to bend something into a curved shape
cards.colloc: curl your finger · curl up · curling smoke
cards.example: The ‘come here’ sign is made by ___ your finger towards you.

cards.def: to say something that upsets or embarrasses somebody without meaning to
cards.colloc: really put your foot in it · put my foot in it again
cards.example: Can you remember a conversation when you ___?

cards.def: to like somebody as soon as you meet them
cards.colloc: hit it off straight away · hit it off with a colleague
cards.example: Can you tell me about a person you ___ with as soon as you met them?
